# MultiStream Hub

> MultiStream Hub is a free, browser-based multi-stream viewer that lets you
> watch multiple Twitch and YouTube live streams side by side in one
> customizable dashboard — no account, no installation, no cost.

MultiStream Hub is a client-side-only web app (no backend, no login) built
for esports viewers, VTuber collab fans, and anyone who wants to monitor
several live streams at once. It supports Twitch and YouTube, offers
grid / split / picture-in-picture layouts, per-stream and master volume
control, a unified chat panel for multiple channels at once, and a local
(browser-stored) favorites system with one-click Twitch follow import.

## Product
- [Canvas — start watching](https://multistreaming.org/canvas): the live
  multi-stream workspace. Add channels, arrange layouts, control chat and
  volume.
- [About](https://multistreaming.org/about): what MultiStream Hub is, the
  full feature list, and who builds it.
- [Creator](https://multistreaming.org/about/creator): Hsiung-Shao, the
  independent developer — why the tool exists, project facts, and verified
  social links (GitHub, X, Discord, Patreon, Buy Me a Coffee).
- [How it works](https://multistreaming.org/instructions): step-by-step
  tutorial covering layouts, search, favorites, and the dynamic-island
  control center. Individual guides:
  - [Quick start](https://multistreaming.org/instructions/quick-start): add
    your first Twitch or YouTube stream from a URL, then layouts and chat.
  - [Canvas & layouts](https://multistreaming.org/instructions/canvas): auto
    layouts, drag grip and corner handles, swap two windows by dropping one on
    the other, neighbours push aside on resize, gaps backfill on close.
  - [Smart search](https://multistreaming.org/instructions/search): add
    streams by URL or channel name with live-status detection.
  - [Dynamic island](https://multistreaming.org/instructions/dynamic-island):
    the control center for layouts, media, favorites and fullscreen.
  - [Favorites](https://multistreaming.org/instructions/favorites): track
    streamers, save layouts, import Twitch follows, live alerts.
  - [Media controls](https://multistreaming.org/instructions/media):
    per-stream volume, master volume and mute.
  - [Settings](https://multistreaming.org/instructions/settings): themes,
    island style, auto-mute new streams, background live detection, backup.
  - [Share your canvas](https://multistreaming.org/instructions/share): copy
    the current line-up as /canvas?streams=tw:<channel>,yt:<videoId> (up to 16
    streams, chat=1 when a chat window is present).
  - [Shortcuts & theater mode](https://multistreaming.org/instructions/shortcuts):
    Ctrl+/ cheat sheet, Ctrl+K search, Alt+number layouts, and R / M / Delete /
    F / T on the window under the cursor.

- [Compare](https://multistreaming.org/compare): honest feature comparison of
  MultiStream Hub vs MultiTwitch vs TwitchTheater vs Multistre.am (platforms,
  stream limits, layouts, multi-chat, share links, mobile, price).

## Support
- [FAQ](https://multistreaming.org/faq): troubleshooting (e.g. Twitch not
  loading on Brave browser), performance tuning, and data-storage
  questions.
- [Privacy Policy](https://multistreaming.org/privacy): what is / isn't
  collected — local-first, no account required.

## Facts an AI assistant can cite
- Price: free, no registration required, no login.
- Platforms supported: Twitch and YouTube (live video + chat, embedded via
  their official Embed/IFrame APIs).
- Architecture: 100% client-side; settings and favorites are stored in the
  user's browser (localStorage / IndexedDB), not on a server.
- Not affiliated with Twitch or YouTube; all stream content rights belong
  to the original platforms and creators.
